visual_goal: Show money signals coming from control totals and ledger balances, not sampled traces; the collector carries them alongside traces, alerts are routed by financial flow to the owner who can act, and the same numbers become daily control evidence.
prompt: A left-to-right flow illustration. Every label is written exactly once, directly below its icon. At the far left, four small boxes stacked vertically: 'Payments', 'Subledger', 'Ledgers' and 'Bank', each with one arrow right into an open book labeled 'Delivery ledger'. Next, one arrow from the book into a calculator with a few coins beside it, labeled 'Money in flight'. From the calculator exactly two arrows leave: one thick arrow right into a pipe junction labeled 'Collector', and one arrow straight down into a filing cabinet with a checkmark labeled 'Evidence'. Directly above the pipe junction sits a small box labeled 'Traces', and a thin dotted line with sparse dots runs straight down from 'Traces' into the pipe junction; 'Traces' connects to nothing else. Next, one arrow from the pipe junction into a switchboard with a small dial gauge labeled 'Alert router'. At the far right, four small desks with a bell on each, stacked vertically, labeled 'Pay team', 'SFP team', 'Close duty' and 'Treasury'; the router sends one arrow to each desk. Exactly thirteen arrows and one dotted line.
alt: Payments, subledger, ledgers and bank statements report control totals into a delivery ledger; a money-in-flight calculator feeds the collector alongside sampled traces and writes daily evidence; an alert router sends each alert to the Pay team, SFP team, close duty or treasury.

visual_goal: Show the quarter-end incident timeline: webhooks rejected by the rate limit and queued for retry, a fallback poll posts reports once, overnight retries trigger the same reports again under new event IDs, and the hourly control total check catches the gap.
prompt: A horizontal timeline across a sky that shifts from dusk on the left to night on the right with a crescent moon, over three horizontal lanes. Top lane: a generic office building labeled 'Provider'. Middle lane: a small machine labeled 'Report loader'. Bottom lane: an open book labeled 'Subledger'. Events from left to right: first, a flurry of envelopes from 'Provider' bounces off a brick wall labeled 'Rate limit' and piles into a tray labeled 'Retry queue'. Next, an arrow labeled 'Fallback poll' goes from 'Report loader' up to the provider and brings back a document stack; one green arrow drops from the loader into the subledger labeled 'Posted once'. Next, under the moon, the queued envelopes fly through the wall, and the loader fetches the same document stack again; one red arrow drops into the subledger labeled 'Posted twice', with the second stack carrying different tag colors. At the far right, a magnifying glass with a ringing alarm bell over the subledger, labeled 'Control check', with a red callout reading '186,240 lines'.
alt: Timeline from evening to night: provider webhooks bounce off the rate limit into a retry queue, a fallback poll posts the reports once, overnight retries cause the same reports to be fetched and posted a second time, and the hourly control check flags 186,240 lines.

visual_goal: Show the financial incident path: restore appears only on the branch where no event log can rebuild the data; every path ends in a reconciliation that proves the result before evidence and notification.
prompt: A left-to-right path of compact rounded stations along a single track. At the far left a station with an alarm bell labeled 'Detect', one arrow into a diamond labeled 'Money affected?'. Above the diamond a small grey box labeled 'Technical process' reached by one short grey arrow up. One arrow from the diamond right into a station with a pause button labeled 'Contain', then one arrow into a station with a magnifying glass over an open ledger labeled 'Assess'. From 'Assess' the track forks into two stacked branches: on top a wide green box with a curved undo arrow labeled 'Reversal and re-post'; below it a smaller grey box with a broken chain icon labeled 'Restore: no event log'. Each branch sends one arrow into a highlighted station with two matching checkmarks labeled 'Prove by reconciliation'. Then one arrow into a station with a filing cabinet labeled 'Evidence', one arrow into a station with an envelope labeled 'Notify', and one arrow into a station with a meeting table labeled 'Review' at the far right. Exactly eleven arrows.
alt: Incident path from Detect through a money check (non-financial incidents go to the technical process), Contain and Assess, forking into reversal and re-post or, only with no event log, restore; both branches converge on proof by reconciliation, then evidence, notification and review.
